Chemical engineering interactive simulation library

Research, scientific models and software contracts for a reusable teaching library, from an equation on a lecture slide to a comparison with a physical experiment.

Find a simulationResearch and standardsMeasured-data exampleSources

What to build first

Build one composite wall and one pipe contraction in the same browser runtime. The wall tests whether students can separate a material property from a geometric change. Continuity tests whether the same interface can enforce a physical constraint in a different system.

Then publish the hydraulic learning pathway through to pump and system curves. The pump operating point ranked first for Furmtech because it connects a high-value design decision with two existing FlexBench practicals. Each model has its own version; an instructor can change the activity, lock a variable or collect a prediction without forking the scientific calculation.

84 simulation specifications · 28 prototype coding briefs · 11 subject areas · 12 prioritisation criteria. All records are specification drafts. Numerical reference checks and a measured-data regression example are included. External subject review, browser implementation and validation against the physical rig remain open.

Research and standards

Research and educational design

Benchmark assessment and curriculum evidence

What the evidence supports

Undergraduate resources already let students change parameters, observe flows and temperatures, step equilibrium stages and collect virtual data. LearnChemE even distinguishes simulations, self-study and digital experiments. Paying for a second interface to the same calculation is a weak proposition. The testable Furmtech proposition is continuity of evidence across a lesson: ask for a prediction, identify the governing assumptions, save exactly what was calculated, then explain a discrepancy against a recorded physical run. The first sales or teaching pilot should measure whether academics actually use that chain. No market-size or purchasing-intent estimate follows from this review. [LEARN, VIRTUAL, PHET, TRAY]

Curriculum evidence and scope

Evidence reviewed What it supports Design consequence
University of Melbourne curriculum note and departmental course-coordinator pack [MELB] Fluid mechanics and process/control pathways; different undergraduate-to-professional pathways make year labels institution-specific. The internal note flags handbook access and uses indirect evidence for some claims. Label prerequisites by skill. Offer head balance as a lecture, worked tutorial and pre-lab before using pump data.
RMIT internal curriculum note and current chemical engineering programme page [RMIT] Laboratory and integrated engineering context. The note explicitly distinguishes course scope from inferred equipment. Provide a manual-only scenario, anonymised CSV and lab-report output. Do not attribute a particular pump or experiment to the institution without confirmation.
Monash CHE2163 and CHE3167 [MON2, MON] plus internal Monash curriculum note Heat/mass transfer and later transport/numerical methods make a shared transport example useful at two levels. Link steady slab to transient slab and mesh study. Keep level selectable in a recipe.
UQ chemical engineering study plan and dated internal mapping [UQ] The internal mapping links CHEE3004 unit operations, CHEE3005 reaction engineering and CHEE3007 modelling/control. The public plan documents a cohort pathway. Connect one tank balance to reaction, tracer and control activities. Verify a particular cohort before mapping to assessment.
MIT 10.302 syllabus and Lamm/Jarboe preface [MIT, SEP] Transport and computational prerequisites for separations; reinforces progression to unit operation design. Introduce mass-transfer driving force before packed absorber sizing, phase equilibrium before stage design.

This is a purposive cross-section and a curriculum fit assessment. Counts of course occurrences, student difficulty and willingness to pay have not been measured. Academic levels in the register are Furmtech teaching recommendations. Internal sources used were the four named curriculum Markdown notes and EXP01 through EXP04 drafts, read directly. No university endorsement or equipment inventory is inferred.

Evidence to teaching design

Freeman et al. aggregate undergraduate STEM active-learning evidence; the finding supports using a simulation in an active task, not promising a specific score improvement for this product [ACTIVE]. Adams et al. investigate students using simulations and motivate trials of discoverability and representational clarity [DESIGN]. Mayer and Moreno support segmenting explanation and coordinating relevant words and graphics [LOAD]. Karpicke and Roediger support requiring retrieval after exposure; their experimental context differs from engineering-design assessment [RETRIEVE]. Accordingly, collect an initial prediction, have the student explain a surprising case, then pose a later transfer problem without the first worked solution. Conduct a local pilot before making efficacy claims.

Validation of the product hypothesis

Pilot the same published model in a lecture and pre-lab, on at least two device classes, with one physical or archived teaching run. Ask academics to configure it without an engineer. Record which controls they hide, whether the prediction survives handoff, time to compare data, and whether the learner can explain a held-out discrepancy. Compare a matched static worked example where feasible, collect baseline preparation and disclose small sample limitations. Pilot outcomes are evidence about usability and learning transfer; sales evidence requires separate conversations about procurement and support.

Learning activities, progressive disclosure and assessment

Start with a physical question whose answer could plausibly go two ways. Put the selected variable, diagram feature, graph marker and equation term in the same focus group. Introduce a second mechanism after a student can describe the first one. Present controls in pairs only when their mathematical roles are different and visible. A typical 15-minute investigation allocates 2 minutes to prediction, 4 to controlled changes, 4 to interpretation, 3 to assumption checking and 2 to retrieval in a new context. A lecture can use only the first three minutes.

Mode What the learner does What is recorded Example using the wall
Explore Change one physical quantity and compare to a pinned state Optional bookmarked state and units Drag thickness and conductivity separately, locate where slope changes.
Investigate Commit direction and reason, vary one factor, interpret observed magnitude Prediction before reveal, both states and explanation Double first-layer thickness. Quantify the fraction of resistance it originally provided.
Challenge Work to a target or diagnose an unfamiliar result, document exclusions Design basis, candidates, validity and a claim with evidence Meet a heat-flux ceiling under a thickness cap and explain a measured interface jump.

Introductory preset exposes two controls and the diagram. Intermediate adds term highlighting, a shared plot and the assumptions panel. Advanced unlocks parameter dependence, fit, inverse problem and uncertainty, as separate author choices. An instructor can choose independent operation without overlays. Transfer checks change constraints, units or boundary conditions rather than just substituting new numbers. A knowledge check gives feedback tied to the mechanism and allows another attempt after an explanation. A student can skip motion and inspect the numerical table.

Assessment rubric for an open design. Award 0–2 each for a correct balance with units, physical interpretation, model applicability, feasible design/alternative and validation reasoning. A correct numeric answer alone earns at most the calculation component. Preserve ungraded prediction history. For a short lecture, evaluate an exit question orally; grade passback is a later host feature. [ACTIVE, RETRIEVE, LOAD, DESIGN]

Student interface and accessible visualisation

Desktop places the physical scene and result above the equation and trend; controls form an adjacent column. Tablet stacks a short control group below the scene. At 320 CSS pixels use one column, numeric entry and a list/table alternative to pan-dependent plots. Keep the selected input and its principal output simultaneously visible where possible. Example S11 desktop orders title/objective, slab scene, heat flux, thickness/conductivity controls, equation, resistance chart and optional investigation. On mobile move the heat flux and edited control into the immediate reading order; keep a persistent pause button during animation.

Element Interaction contract
Controls Native labels, units adjacent, numeric field equivalent to slider, keyboard arrows and coarse/fine steps. Allow editing partial tokens; commit on Enter/blur, show last calculated value while invalid. Range and fixed/derived state announced.
Units SI engine; localised display labels. Separate absolute and gauge pressure, differential and absolute T, mole and mass fractions, Darcy and Fanning factors. Preserve full precision in exports and return to exact SI on display switch.
Equation Render symbolic line, numeric substitution with units, contributions and rounded answer. Term activation via focus/click links to the corresponding control, plot marker and scene element. Include accessible linear text and a plain-text worked example.
Scene Pipes/tanks/slabs carry physical dimensions. Distinguish mean from local velocity; a thin wall or boundary layer can be magnified only with axis label. A continuum law does not predict individual particle paths. Direction by arrows, scale by numeric legend.
Plot Named axes with units and reference state. Use shared axes for comparisons, separate incompatible units, distinct dashes and point shapes. For zero/negative values on log scales explain exclusion. No joined line between independent measurements by default.
Motion Pause/play, step and reset always available; user-controlled 0.25×–4× display speed. Respect reduced motion. No autoplay required for an answer. Changing animation speed leaves solver and assessment invariant.
Status Icon + text + specific rule; describes consequence and next possible model. Screen reader announces a concise committed change, not every animation frame.
Export Accessible data table, CSV and replayable JSON; label synthetic, measured, assumed or fitted. Suppress unknown derived values while preserving their reason.

WCAG 2.2 AA target: test keyboard order and visible focus, name/role/value, 200% zoom and reflow, contrast (4.5:1 ordinary text, 3:1 relevant graphics and large text), target size, alternatives to dragging, pause and reduced motion. Use solid/dashed curves with symbols; status must remain readable in monochrome. Test a complete S11 investigation with keyboard and screen reader, a pump duty selection with touch only and every plot via a table, including an out-of-range point. Colour legend units and minimum/maximum are mandatory. Reference [WCAG].

Scientific standards and equipment design

Model fidelity and maturity
Tag Representation Decision and evidence
F1 Fundamental analytical Exact under declared idealisation; check units and analytical limits.
F2 Extended analytical Several mechanisms, geometry, effective parameters or boundary conditions; verify each term.
F3 Empirical or semi-empirical Name data source, coefficient convention, geometry, fitted range and uncertainty.
F4 Numerical Declare solver, stopping criteria, refinement, initialisation and error evidence.
F5 Specialist computational Document spatial problem, mesh, time resolution, closures, boundary data and independent verification.
F6 Calibrated or hybrid Record equipment identity, calibration domain, fit and held-out validation data.

Tags may coexist and attach to a variant. A root finder for Colebrook adds an F4 algorithm to an F3 law. Blasius is a similarity model solved as an ODE; it does not become a full CFD flow field. A synthetic example with a future rig curve is F2 in starter mode; F6 becomes active only when an identified calibration is loaded. S77 teaches discretisation; F5 labels a comparison target for specialist models. Freeze the variant in every saved scenario. A small time step cannot fix a guessed heat-transfer coefficient. Prioritise improving the dominant source of error for the decision being made.

For an upgrade, write the target quantity and required tolerance, missing mechanism, cost of new inputs/solver, and method for checking improvement on independent data. Reject an upgrade if it is unidentifiable from the measurements or fails to improve the engineering decision. Pair every maturity stamp with a version, scope of claim and reviewer. A verified F1 can outperform an uncalibrated F6.

Applicability, missing data and extrapolation

Each rule stores a stable ID, variant, fact being tested, source and locator, kind (physical constraint, empirical domain, product guard, missing evidence, numerical condition), inclusive/exclusive bounds, units, reason, effect on outputs, alternative and ownership. Output eligibility is per quantity: a calculated Reynolds number can remain meaningful when a friction-factor estimate is suppressed. Formula choices and screen ranges are separately versioned. Treat unspecified geometry or boundary state as unknown. Cap numerical controls for interaction without treating those caps as a scientific domain.

Status UI treatment Action
Within documented applicability Check icon, text and applicable rule list All required known conditions pass. Explain evidence and omitted effects.
Approaching a limit Triangle and labelled condition Show distance in physical units. Each rule carries an explicit source or author-defined buffer.
Outside documented applicability Stop marker, offending fact and consequence Suppress affected normal output, export null plus reason; prevent assessed credit. For authorised educational extrapolation render separate dashed estimate and watermark.
Cannot establish applicability Question icon and missing fact Block design recommendation that depends on it; show conditional calculations only with assumptions visible.

Combine controlling rules in order outside → unknown → approaching → within, retaining every individual result. Computational failure is a separate error channel. Solver convergence and model validity are independent. Example: full pipe, Newtonian fluid, sufficient development and fixed properties are separate checks; Re alone cannot establish the pipe model. In S05, screen 2000–<2300 as approaching, 2300–4000 transitional and above that outside the laminar teaching envelope. In S08 use approach band 2000–<2300 and 4000–4500 as provisional UI buffers, not physical thresholds. For S06, warn from Reₓ 4×10⁵, suppress laminar teaching prediction past 5×10⁵ unless instructor explicitly chooses comparison. Surface disturbance must be specified or labelled assumed. For S13 disclose Bi=0.1 screen, geometry, IC and face conditions. The catalogue preset may explicitly stipulate an ideal boundary condition; for user data, require evidence or return unknown.

A comparison card reports both model names, boundary conditions, common units and inputs, curve provenance, absolute difference and relative difference where the denominator is meaningful. Preserve all invalidity flags in CSV and screenshots. Prohibit interpolation across a transition gap. Correlation coefficients without original fit range or geometry may be used in labelled synthetic exercises; numerical recommendations for an actual service require review.

Empirical correlations and boundaries

The admissibility dimension includes source, geometry, independent-variable convention, fluid class, original data range, uncertainty, and alternative law. A teaching slider range never serves as the original data range. Unknown fields suppress the “within documented applicability” claim for real-service design. The following dispositions apply to all referenced blocks. Unquoted coefficients and algebra are written in the corresponding scientific specifications; published figures, tables and datasets are not bundled.

Record and provenance Basis, coefficients and conditions Range, uncertainty, extrapolation and substitute
Pipe Darcy friction [COLE, ROUGH, DOE], S08 Colebrook implicit law, uniform fully developed turbulent Newtonian flow in circular rough pipe. ε/D and pipe Re; 2.51 and 3.7 with base-10 log, Darcy convention. Historical roughened pipe evidence. Teaching gate 4×10³–10⁷ and ε/D≤.05; this is an implementation envelope. Original specimen range/error bound needs independent extraction before claiming generic fit accuracy. Use laminar 64/Re where appropriate; transition unresolved, measured pressure drop for actual pipe.
Flat-plate momentum [BLASIUS, BL], S06 Blasius similarity and computed constants Cf,x≈.664/√Reₓ, Cfavg≈1.328/√ReL. These follow from the similarity solution and are not fitted equipment coefficients. Edge defined at u/U=.99. Smooth zero-pressure-gradient attached laminar geometry, no universal transition Re or universal uncertainty. Compare collocation, pressure-gradient solution or measured field.
Isothermal plate heat transfer [POHL, HEAT], S14 Local .332 and average .664 times Re^½Pr^⅓; compact approximation to similarity solution for laminar forced convection. Use conductivity of the fluid; evaluate real properties at stated film temperature. Pr=.6–10 as conservative teaching subset, Re bounded by plate transition rule; full source fit-error envelope pending reviewer. Very low Pr, mixed convection or heated-start offset need new models; compare S06 thermal BVP.
Packed-bed pressure drop [ERGUN], S50 150 and 1.75 terms in superficial velocity, particle size and voidage. This combines viscous/inertial terms for a packed bed. Sphere preset and incipient fluidisation use separate force balance. Voidage, size distribution, particle shape and wall effects matter. Confirm primary fit envelope/error against original article before quantitative service use. Alternative measured packing curve.
Sphere heat/mass transfer [RM], S83 2+.6 Re^½ Sc^⅓ or Pr^⅓, isolated particle and external-fluid properties. Original evaporation experiments concern drops. Do not generalise drop evaporation to dense beds or large evaporation rates. Original article range and uncertainty not established from bibliographic retrospective. Research-only for external-duty design, compare pure diffusion limit Sh=2.
Pump, valve, meter, mixing [PUMP, IEC, PERRY], S09/S42/S47/S75 H=s²H₀−aQ², Q=CdA₂√(…), valve G(x) or Np in P=NpρN³D⁵. Coefficients in the pack are illustrative, not vendor coefficients. Synthetic defaults have no calibration uncertainty or fluid applicability claim. Require instrument/impeller ID, actual geometry, speed/viscosity window, a fitted dataset and withheld run. Use manufacturer data or a verified plant-specific curve.
Binary volatility / kinetics [SEP, IUPAC, FOG, MONOD, MM], S19–23/S41/S70–73 Constant α and synthetic saturation pressures; Margules parameter, Arrhenius kref,Ea, growth and enzyme saturation parameters are scenario-specific. Default is a teaching construction. Identify mixture/reaction and fit ranges before selecting a physical model. Alternatives are measured VLE, activity/fugacity models and expanded kinetics with independent data.
Adsorption, filtration and membrane [LANG, FILTER, VMAX, PERRY], S24/S62/S63/S78/S82 Langmuir b,qmax, medium resistance, specific cake resistance, empirical capacity and mass-transfer coefficients are material/feed dependent. No inherited coefficient validity across feeds/pressure/membranes. Check data fit and prediction intervals, cross-flow versus dead-end and compressibility; compare alternate resistance models and measured endpoints.
Antoine/property fits [NIST, NISTTERMS], later variants log10(P in declared source unit)=A−B/(T+C), source T convention fixed. Data records include CAS/source/temperature interval and permitted use. Coefficients for different ranges and units cannot be spliced silently. Actual WebBook records are linked, no coefficient table shipped. Check overlap, endpoints and redistribution terms.
Empirical teaching regression [STAT, STRD, NORRIS], S27 Training and independent validation, units, x range, synthetic source flag or data provenance. Includes residuals, confidence/prediction intervals. Assumptions on noise and design matter; extrapolation remains flagged even for a high R². Norris reference values are −.262323073774029 for the intercept and 1.00211681802045 for the slope are calculation benchmarks, not rig data.

Correlation manifest requires original citation, equation identifier, parameter values and units, coefficient provenance, fitted materials/geometry, documented joint domain, property evaluation convention, uncertainty if reported or explicit unknown, alternative and data-rights decision. A cited handbook is a locator; engineering sign-off must inspect the actual correlation and original conditions.

Additional source qualification

IAEA’s Sodium Coolant Handbook, table 31, gives a secondary reference envelope for the Colebrook–White form of 4×10³ to 10⁸ in Re and relative roughness up to .05. Furmtech deliberately narrows the upper Re to 10⁷ for the teaching controls. The handbook envelope is not an error guarantee for student pipework. IAEA table 31 · Colebrook original

The Ergun original is indexed by UCSF and explicitly investigates flow, fluid, voidage and granular-solid characteristics. The published retrospective for Ranz and Marshall identifies drop diameters of 0.06–0.11 cm and air temperatures extending to 220 °C across the experiments. These are descriptions of the experimental programme, not blanket operating limits for every equation or fluid. Ergun original record · Ranz–Marshall retrospective

R-MOL Molar gas constant 8.314462618 J/(mol K), rounded Physical constant, rounded as stated All temperatures absolute.
TEACH-WATER Density 1000 kg/m³, μ=.001 Pa·s when stated in module Constant illustrative hydraulic inputs, original fixtures No claim of simultaneous precision at a specific water state. Gauge/absolute pressure and cavitation checks separate.
TEACH-PLATE ν=1.5e−5 m²/s, kf=.026 W/(m K), selectable Pr Illustrative property set Pr must be calculated if μ, cp and k are independently supplied; independent Pr slider is a dimensionless teaching family.
TEACH-WALL User-defined positive conductivity and resistance Generic specimen parameters with declared bounds Thickness is geometric. A material change affects k; apparent k can also reflect contact/heterogeneity.
TEACH-BINARY Fixed illustrative Psat pair 200 and 100 kPa Synthetic binary at one unspecified fixed teaching temperature No named mixture, temperature sweep or physical validation.
WEBBOOK Component identity, property, phase, citation, range, unit convention [NIST] Link to source; verify NIST SRD terms before bundling coefficients [NISTTERMS] Do not extrapolate or claim all US government data are unrestricted.
NORRIS Ozone-monitor calibration data, NIST StRD [STRD, NORRIS] Publicly accessible reference dataset and certified coefficients, linked, not repackaged Independent software check for regression, not FlexBench validation.
EXP01–04 Furmtech experiment designs for pump, system/valve, series/parallel and PID Internal documents used for alignment. Runtime data absent. Require permission/provenance, actual CSV, geometry, timebase, instrument quality and separate held-out run.

Later property packs must specify phase, p/T validity, species, composition basis, property uncertainty, interpolation method and units, source/licence and revision. Include independent property checkpoints, boundary queries and continuity test across adjacent fit intervals. Missing pressure, temperature or mixture tags return unknown. Choosing a nominal teaching fluid is an explicit assumed fact in the session. An imported file never inherits the provenance of a source merely because column names match.

Performance, inverse design and optimisation

Design basis. Record service, geometry and orientation, imposed flows/temperatures/pressures, allowable losses and constraints, operating window, property source and uncertainty, candidate catalogue revision and duty schedule. Identify which variables the user can set in each mode. The forward solver is the source of truth. After solving an inverse problem, re-run the forward model on the rounded, available candidate and on operating-window extremes.

Mode Algorithm Required output
Performance Evaluate a given candidate at a prescribed input state Duty, losses, utilities, validity and relevant margin; plot basis and units.
Design Invert analytically, bracket physically separated roots, or enumerate a discrete catalogue All admissible candidates, no solution, unique solution, multiple branches or missing evidence. Include active constraints and residual.
Optimisation Enumerate or sample feasible controls, eliminate dominated candidates and show trade-off Pareto set on stated objectives, robustness under changed inputs, reason each rejected candidate fails. Never silently choose weights.

Worked duty. S10 at Q=.001 m³/s, D=.05 m and the published illustrative constants yields about 2.132 m required head and 34.85 W shaft power. At .025 m the velocity exceeds the default 2 m/s ceiling. A .063 m bore saves friction head but adds diameter. Put both surviving and rejected points on the plot. For annual energy convert shaft power using actual motor efficiency and operating hours. Where prices are absent, plot diameter, kWh and water use. If pricing is supplied, record AUD/base year, source, assumed installation scope, replacement life, annual hours, tariff, discount rate and sensitivity. Lifecycle present worth equals initial capital plus sum of annual net costs discounted to the basis date. Do not infer capex from diameter alone.

Equipment Geometry that changes Performance, inverse and trade-off Next engineering evidence
Pipe / pump / valve Actual bore, head duty, valve throat Pressure drop / bore and speed / power vs size and operating range Manufacturer curves, allowable duty, NPSH margin, system hydraulics, service/material rating; valve standard [IEC].
Exchanger / insulation Area, equivalent tube length, inner/outer radii Duty / area or thickness / approach vs fouling, energy vs clearance Actual pass configuration, fouling history, pressure drop, mechanical rating, vibration and thermal expansion [HEAT].
Reactor / residence vessel / mixer Working volume, diameter, impeller and headspace Conversion or mixing / V,N / yield, energy and residence distribution Verified kinetics, mixing trials, heat removal, containment and review of process hazards.
Distillation / absorption Theoretical contacts, packing height and diameter Separation / stage count, area or height / utility vs size Actual tray efficiency, packing curves, hydraulics/flooding, pressure rating, vendor and professional design.
Cake filter / membrane / centrifuge Effective area, module count, equivalent settling area Throughput / area or capacity / installation vs cleaning and recovery Service trials, membrane limits, cycle overhead, cut curve and equipment ratings.
Utilities / resource use Capacity, peak demand, storage working volume Energy balance / supply or buffer / energy, water and cost Duty coincidence, operating schedule, local tariff, reliability and supply limits.

These are preliminary teaching scopes. An equipment requirement record must identify applicable local design codes, required vendor selections and professional review; certified pressure boundaries, relief sizing, protective trips and plant safety cases are separate engineering deliverables. Avoid a universal design margin. If an educator specifies a factor, show its basis, effect on feasibility and units. A missing vendor datum is an explicit unknown.

Scientific verification and physical validation

For each variant freeze source edition and equation locator, signs and units, independent/derived inputs, initial and boundary values, fit range, numerical error target, reference fixture and a short physical explanation. An equation or a matching spreadsheet does not validate equipment behaviour. Retain a reviewer separate from the implementer for scientific sign-off where feasible.

Gate Evidence and pass conditions Failure action
Research concept → specification drafted A–P complete at declared depth; outcome, planned data origin, visual mapping, missing data and scope explicit Return to author with specific gaps
Mathematical model verified Subject reviewer checks derivation, assumptions, physical dimensions; second-method benchmark, zero/limit/boundary cases; conservation, residual and refinement evidence Quarantine variant or narrow documented scope
Prototype implemented Frozen fixtures run through normal public block API in browser and worker where applicable, independently of this pack’s reference worksheet Correct implementation or versioned fixture after documented review
Educational review completed Academic and learners complete prediction, investigation and transfer on desktop/mobile and text-only equivalent; identify misleading visuals or feedback Update educational wrapper independently; rerun affected tasks
Released educational simulation Numerical and UI gates, accessibility and browser evidence, licence inventory, exact model/schema versions, rollback and archived scenario replay No public release until open critical issues close
Experimentally validated for defined service Held-out independent run(s), complete instruments/geometry/uncertainty, documented domain and acceptance limits, reviewer and date Retain a verification-only claim or qualify domain

Tolerance policy. For well-conditioned closed forms compare unrounded values to a high-precision independent result using |e|≤max(atol,rtol×|reference|), default rtol=10⁻⁸ and dimensioned atol set per output (1e−8 of a documented characteristic scale unless a stricter fixture exists). Printed examples have their own rounding tolerance in reference_checks.py. Bracketed solves require both residual and bracket/step criteria; scaled residual ≤1e−9 and relative width ≤1e−8 for normalised well-conditioned cases; limits have separate branches. Clamp floating-point roundoff only within a documented tolerance. Unreachable targets, rank failure and no bracket are expected return types. Require balance residual below 1e−8 of transported amount for closed analytic models. For numerical transients use a documented mesh/time study, e.g. relative change <0.5% in quantity of interest on successive independent refinements plus <0.1% normalised balance error as provisional tolerances. Tighten or justify per model; numerical agreement cannot eliminate model-form uncertainty.

Tests that must survive an edit. SI↔︎display round trip; no negative absolute temperature or absolute pressure; stagnation and zero driving force; equal capacities and equal terminal temperatures; sensible output as flow approaches zero; stationary marker and field linked to identical model revision; no stale result after worker cancellation; transition and unknown conditions on both sides; direct vs inverse round trip; compare a saved/pinned academic activity after an upgrade. Exercise touchscreen/keyboard, screen reader, missing external assets, unsupported variants, offline availability, malformed/unitless CSV and synthetic/measured origin. A tie or multiple inverse answers must remain visible.

Physical validation protocol. Define a prediction, service envelope and quantity-specific tolerance before collecting holdout data. Record instrument calibration/resolution, tap elevation and bore, replicates, units and time alignment. Separate calibration and validation by run/day/equipment condition as appropriate, never by adjacent rows from one run. Plot observed vs predicted with measurement bars, residual vs flow, time and other operating variables; report bias, RMSE, conditional uncertainty, number and coverage of independent runs. Account for covariance for quantities formed from shared instruments. A normalised residual using combined standard uncertainty is appropriate only when independence/covariance and uncertainty basis are justified. Assess practical impact on the target learning/design decision. Revalidate after geometry, sensor, curve, range or material-property changes. Simulation-only and synthetic runs cannot establish physical validation.

Pack audit. reference_checks.py is executable independent arithmetic for all 28 prototype topics. Its checked outputs are recorded in reference_results.json. These are spec checks using SciPy/NumPy or direct identities. They do not represent tests of a browser product, human peer review or rig validation. Variant-specific acceptance includes the limiting and invalid cases in each controlled brief. Archive original source, method and tolerance whenever a fixture changes.

Numerical workload and solver acceptance
Blocks Kernel and computational order Convergence, failure and graphics checks
S01–05, S07, S11, S12 forward, S19–22, S24 forward/inverse O(1) scalar arithmetic; O(P) for P plot samples Confirm a reference value, a limiting case and a rejected combination per brief. Keep signs and units at intermediate steps. Use 121 points for smooth 1D charts, include exact discontinuities/endpoints, resize without changing outputs.
S06, S14 comparison Similarity ODE integration O(MN) for M shooting iterations and N η steps. Cache by Pr/domain/tolerance, not x Check f′(0)=0, f′(∞)≈1, f″(0)=.332057±.00002, θ(0)=0/θ(∞)≈1, Pr=1 identity, and δ99 against interpolation from refined solution. S14 direct mean/local law is O(1).
S08 O(log(initial bracket width / tolerance)) per root; O(P×iterations) for a Moody curve At Q=0 f is undefined and Δp=0. Use a residual criterion and bracket-width criterion. Compare same dimensionless state in both dimensional views.
S09–10 Closed synthetic intersection O(1); discrete sizing O(B) for B bores, O(B×iterations) if friction root included Test shutoff, negative-flow exclusion, no crossing, coincident roots and data hull. Importing a new curve invalidates cached intersections.
S12 inverse At most two monotone brackets, each O(log(1/tol)) Report all feasible roots, tangent duplicates once, impossible target separately. Check forward heat-loss residual for each root.
S13 Uniform formula O(1); N-cell backward Euler tridiagonal solve O(N) per step and O(N) working memory Volume-weighted energy balance includes face resistance. Compare e.g. N=40/80/160 and Δt/2 separately. Target <1% difference in centre and mean over selected test cases, then qualify against a reference plane-wall eigenfunction or independent solver.
S15–16 Direct performance and LMTD inverse O(1); design sweep O(B) Cr→1, zero duty, both layout asymptotes, nonpositive ΔTlm arguments; confirm heat balance and re-evaluate design area with forward model.
S17–18 O(1) analytical or erfc per probe; gravity-drain event solve O(steps + bracket iterations) Test t=0 boundary discontinuity; finite slab and half-space are different models. Localise tank-empty/full event, do not silently clip.
S23 O(stages) per R, capped at 500 stage steps; sweep O(B×stages) Verify pinch/finite count and partial reboiler convention. Disable candidate operation past feed-pinch or invalid stage crossing. Show progress/cancel on large sweeps.
S25–26 O(n) scalar steps plus O(n) history unless downsampled in view Fixed sample order, clipped final step and deterministic pause/replay. At refinement compare physical times, quantify divergence separately from overflow.
S27 QR O(np²), p≤3; O(P) prediction band; keep data untouched on failures Rank deficiency and insufficient df must suppress intervals. Holdout used only for evaluation in a declared comparison; reserve separate final test if selecting degree on holdout. Check actual NIST coefficients in NORRIS_COMPARISON.md.
S28 O(1) delta method; O(N) draws and O(N log N) quantile sort Compare variance and mean with analytical first-order scenario at small uncertainties; use multiple seeds or estimated simulation MC error, not deterministic equality with the linearised result for nonlinear Q. Test r=±1 and zero covariance.

These targets define implementation acceptance; no browser timing has yet been measured. Cases outside the scoped implementation are exposed as unavailable variants, not selectable buttons without a supported calculation.

Independent-method review and evidence gaps

The review used independent numerical formulations for selected prototype outputs, machine checks on schemas and examples, and a second reading across sections. No external subject-matter reviewer was engaged; no human peer-review or experimental-validation stamp is issued.

Check Finding or correction Disposition
Velocity, pressure and pipe sizing Checked diameter/area convention, Pa vs metres of head and that the sizing fixture uses the declared 20 m line and Darcy f=.02. Consistent design and reference fixture.
Pump evidence Speed-command data do not establish RPM or efficiency; measured flow head also depends on tap heights and bores. Preserve these dependencies in EXP01/02 import and exclude unsupported power claims.
Boundary layer Independent collocation solution checks wall slope and 99% edge against shooting target. ReL is length-based; physical averages apply to the coefficient or stress. Quantitative separation/turbulent near-wall predictions disabled in laminar branch.
Wall and exchanger Shared flux across series layers and the contact jump checked. Near equal-capacity and equal-temperature-difference limits avoid cancellation. Fixed-face wall vs bath vs two-stream boundary cases explicitly separated.
Stage counting Independent stage stepping gives six equilibrium contacts for S23 default and Rmin=.8. Partial reboiler included, total condenser excluded.
Regression and propagation Checked regression residual norm with independent polynomial fitting and covariance using a matrix expression. Certified Norris values linked as optional external fixture; no real calibration data invented.
Source rights Different conditions apply to PhET HTML, Wolfram embeds and previews, LearnChemE linked materials, OCW and NIST SRD. Link/cite by default and clear actual assets prior to distribution.
Curriculum/readiness Internal notes include indirect and cohort-specific evidence. Course-topic alignment does not establish a lab purchase or experimental inventory. Initial teaching levels, scores, hosting and module boundaries are provisional.

Run python verification/reference_checks.py from the pack root with NumPy and SciPy. Compare output with reference_results.json and inspect tolerances. These computations are independent of the proposed TypeScript runtime, which has not been implemented. Schema validation checks structure; an adapter must also enforce registry membership, units, input locks, compatible model/scenario versions and authorised message origin.

Architecture and delivery

Technology choices, modules and repository

Use a static TypeScript application compiled to JavaScript, with a small React view shell, SVG for annotated equipment and modest plots, native HTML inputs/tables, and locally bundled KaTeX with accessible mathematical text. Use Vite to build immutable versioned assets. Never run executable equations from a scenario. Model packages expose pure functions and an optional state integrator. All renderers consume the same calculated values the learner can export. An academic can publish a scenario by configuration; adding a novel physical model still requires reviewed code.

Technology Trade-off across maintenance, speed, numerical accuracy, deployment and access Decision
TypeScript / JavaScript Types catch contract drift, TS compiles away; both use JS binary64 numbers. Types alone cannot check dimensions or physical validity. Small static bundle works on mobile/offline. TS Apache-2.0 [TS]. TS for public interfaces, pure kernels and tests; no heavy runtime required.
React / native custom elements React MIT, maintainable state and accessible DOM; rendering on every simulation tick wastes CPU. Native elements have a host-independent lifecycle but still need accessible controls and styles [REACT, CUSTOM]. React for first shell; expose a thin custom element when a host needs same-page integration. Vue/Svelte viable alternatives; changing view must not change kernels.
SVG / Canvas / WebGL SVG exposes semantic nodes and handles hundreds of elements. Canvas trades DOM semantics for dense raster speed; WebGL has GPU/context variability, no inherent text/keyboard alternative. No scientific accuracy comes from a renderer. SVG first. Use Canvas for dense images/large traces with table equivalents. Use WebGL only after measuring a genuine large-field need; keep CPU reference scene.
Small SVG plots / D3 / Plotly.js D3 scales/shapes modular, ISC [D3]; Plotly.js MIT [PLOT], many trace types/export, larger bundle. Neither guarantees a readable scientific graph on a phone. Use labelled lightweight SVG paths and tables first. Lazy load plotting library only for dense scientific interactions.
KaTeX / MathJax KaTeX MIT [KATEX], fast local typesetting; MathJax Apache-2.0 [MATHJAX], richer features. Both need assistive-technology testing. KaTeX HTML+MathML, plain-text fallback. Assess MathJax if required notation or speech support fails local tests.
Numerical libraries, units, math.js General engines simplify units/matrices but parsing arbitrary expressions complicates reproducibility. Binary64 needs conditioning, residual checks and known benchmarks. Implement small reviewed analytic kernels and dimension maps; use a vetted QR/statistical special-function dependency when necessary. Lock versions and notices.
Web Workers / WASM Workers avoid blocking interaction; structured cloning costs memory. WASM enables compiled solvers; numerical parity, initial payload and mobile memory matter [WASM, WORKER]. Add cancellable worker after profiling. WASM only for a qualified solver/property package. Never make the DOM or a remote service part of the model.
Python / server services SciPy useful for independent reference runs; scientific Python in a browser adds runtime size. Servers add network, availability, privacy and ongoing support costs. CoolProp core and optional backends have different terms [SCIPY, COOL]. Python offline QA/authoring. Precompute versioned specialist fields where interpolation is defensible. Optional queued, cancellable service only for justified F5 jobs with retained reproducible inputs.
Static hosting / iframe / web component Static URLs are easy to version and cache; iframe isolates host CSS/JS, requires a message trust boundary. Web components allow direct DOM integration in trusted hosts [CUSTOM, MSG, OFFLINE]. Static HTTPS, iframe-first for WordPress and LMS, new-tab fallback. Bundle for local web serving or explicit standalone-file export.

Repository contract

Proposed source folders: packages/model-core (registry, parameter graph, SI units), packages/science (properties, correlations, geometry-specific scale definitions), packages/solvers (root, RK, tridiagonal, regression), packages/runtime (clock, events, scenarios, state), packages/views (SVG primitives, charting, math, accessible tables), packages/learning (activities and assessment predicates), packages/adapters (embed, CSV, local host, later LMS), apps/web, simulations// and tests/golden. This delivered tree is its documentation baseline. IDs persist through title and layout changes.

A declaration supplies modes, typed controls, SI bounds, steps, defaults, linked outputs, semantic anchors, fixed inputs, learning scenarios and sources. Use a dependency DAG for derived variables. For inverse problems change the independent-variable set explicitly; never leave a target and a calculated outcome editable together. Apply atomic input batches and reject invalid combinations without partially updating the state. Compute outputs, rule results, plot data and a data summary from one revision. Ignore stale worker results using instanceId + revision. Separate physics clock from requestAnimationFrame; run a bounded number of steps, report backlog/drop render frames without skipping physical integration.

Reuse boundaries. Geometry + unit conversions + Reynolds scales + friction kernel → pipe, network, pump duty and sizing. Slab resistance and terminal temperature helpers → wall, insulation, exchanger and utilities. FOPDT/sampler + optional controller → control tutorials and simulation-only Master playback. Binary equilibrium methods → flash and distillation, with a variant for fixed-T pressure and a separately declared constant-α design surrogate. Same inputs and names are not enough to reuse a model across boundary conditions.

Renderer catalogue. Pipe segment, reducer, elevation marker, tap and vector rake; vessel inventory/ports; radial or planar layer; reactor concentration region; two-stream exchanger with reversible orientation; valve travel and pump icon; dimension line, reference datum and clipped contour fill; arrows with scale; labelled axes, annotated point, interval band and calibration marker. Composite wall and tank are configurable compositions. Blasius profiles, McCabe–Thiele stepping, covariance plots and Levenspiel areas require custom scientific drawings. Specify whether each primitive represents geometry, a measured field, a derived field or a qualitative illustration.

Performance budgets (provisional engineering targets). Cold shell plus one analytic block ≤350 kB compressed JS excluding optional bundled fonts; median input-to-stable-output <50 ms, p95 <100 ms on a documented midrange Android test device. Use 10–20 Hz text/plot updates during motion, ≤30 fps for scene; settle synchronously on keyboard commit. Bound imported CSV to 5 MB/100k rows for first release, downsample only the view, preserve raw data. Worker decision if repeated model work exceeds 16 ms on reference device. Test last two supported releases of Chrome, Edge, Firefox, Safari plus iOS Safari and Android Chrome; print exact tested versions at release.

Function block lifecycle, events and errors

The public contract is in contracts/block.ts. An instance has lifecycle new → ready → running ↔︎ paused → disposed. Analytical blocks calculate in ready/paused; start/advance on an algebraic block returns UNSUPPORTED. On init validate manifest and version then load defaults atomically. Start/resume does not reset. Pause finishes the current model step; reset restores scenario defaults and zero time, begins a new run, clears active history and emits reset. Dispose is idempotent and cancels workers and subscriptions. Any later operation rejects with DISPOSED.

Units and metadata travel with results. Input batches have an optional expected revision for optimistic concurrency. A revision is allocated only after successful validation and commit. Calculation response includes matching revision, namespaced output IDs, status by output, scientific data origins and unit map. Calculation may legitimately return null for unmodelled quantities. Errors are coded, recoverable and distinguish bad input, missing model/asset, incompatible version, empty data, solver failure and cancellation. Commands from hosts carry protocol, exact version, requestId and instanceId; acknowledgements and events are separate. Retry cache keyed by host session and requestId prevents repeated steps or submissions. No state mutation from an obsolete acknowledgement.

Save state includes values, active mode, dynamic state vector, clock/step, pending scheduled events, solver version, seed and generator state, history policy, model/property/correlation versions, learning activity snapshot and any hashes of external data. Save/restore is round-trip deterministic for the declared supported solver build. For cross-browser floating point differences assert scientific tolerances. Loading a scenario validates required anchors/outputs, locks and ranges before initialisation; locked values cannot be changed by learner input. The host may be absent. Activity completion comes from a host-neutral predicate, never a guessed page view.

Event Minimum payload besides common envelope
parameter.changed changed IDs, prior and new SI values, source, revision
calculation.completed outputs, validity, revision and simulated time
simulation.stateChanged from, to, simulated time, run ID
validity.changed affected output, rule IDs, facts, previous and new state
error code, severity, affected input/step, recoverability
activity.completed activity/version, criterion, evidence refs and timestamp
data.exported content kind, schema version, row count, user action; exclude raw personal data

Offline initial site can use the same interface in-process. A static iframe calls it through a constrained adapter. Future Qt Master can load the same versioned bundle in a supported WebEngine view or use a local browser page. Runtime may compare recorded telemetry but has no actuator methods. Physical operation, PLC command authority, interlocks and operating recipes belong in the existing equipment system. The precise desktop adapter depends on review of the actual Master/Author build.

Formats, versioning and repeatability
Object Format and constraints
Manifest and parameter dictionary UTF-8 JSON, JSON Schema 2020-12. Stable model/variant and variable IDs; values finite, SI internal; units explicit per variable, description of temperature and pressure basis.
Scenario JSON schema + registry-aware validation. Exact model/variant version, initial values, allowed controls, narrower bounds, locks, reveal rules, semantic anchors and criterion expression from enumerated operations.
Snapshot Versioned JSON, checksum of source data and profile, RNG/solver state, events and timestamps, independent scenario and learning version. Exact replay or explicit migration receipt.
Numerical outputs and histories Tidy CSV UTF-8 with header, CSV quoting, decimal point, time basis and units in named columns or companion mapping; paired JSON metadata for units, source, quality, model and scenario versions. Empty field with reason for unknown, never a zero substitute.
Experiment Immutable input bytes, content hash, equipment and instrument metadata, calibration date/uncertainty, row quality, planned exclusions and declared split by run. Derived dataset retains parent ID and transformations.
Assessment JSON evidence with prompt version, prediction, tolerance, calculation revision and completion rule. Suppress external submission by default.
Large spatial data Optional compressed binary typed-array field with JSON mesh/units/BC metadata; consider HDF5/NetCDF for specialist offline workflows after a demonstrated need. Link to a validated mesh and provenance.

Version schema and model independently. Use semver and exact pins for published courses; any change affecting a previously assessable numerical response requires a new model version and replay comparison. Never replace an existing published asset in place. Additive metadata migrations are pure, logged and tested. For incompatible changes preserve previous reader or provide clearly stated migration and new verification fixtures.

Synthetic data generator. Define xorshift32 v1 unsigned state, nonzero seed, update by XOR with left shifts 13,17-right-unsigned,5-left in that order, truncating to uint32 each step. Uniform U=(uint32+0.5)/2³². Normals are Box–Muller from successive independent uniforms using sqrt(−2 ln U1)cos(2πU2); discard sine partner in v1 for stable stream. For holdout seed use seed XOR 0x9e3779b9, replace zero with 1. Noise-free fixtures may skip RNG only if documented in snapshot. Initial MC seed 17. Synthetic data uses source=synthetic and explicit generator version/parameters on scene, plot and export. Measured data require acquisition record. A fitted curve retains label fitted even when overlaid on measurements.

Validation order. Parse under size cap, reject unknown schema versions, map required units including affine temperature conversion, require known channel semantics and nonnegative time increments (two equal timestamps require an explicit event or deduplication decision), flag gaps and duplicates, preview, accept without changing raw file. Validate shape, then model-dependent constraints and admissibility. Distinguish “loaded successfully” from “eligible for a quantitative comparison”.

WordPress, offline delivery and LMS

Publish a static catalogue at a first-party HTTPS path or a dedicated subdomain such as sims.furmtech.com.au. Choose the separate origin if DNS and hosting permit; this is a proposed address. WP page holds introduction, objectives, versioned iframe, title and fallback link. The model, solver, fonts and datasets are self-hosted static assets with immutable content hashes. No WP rewrite, PHP numerical computation, user account or analytics service is required. Verify editor permissions and sanitisation because WordPress can strip disallowed iframe markup [WP]. If necessary, provide an administrator-managed shortcode restricted to the Furmtech origin and simulation IDs. Confirm staging behaviour with actual theme, caching plugin and a logged-out mobile visit.

Use versioned paths /sim/S11/1.0.0/ and /scenario//; a catalogue “latest” link may move but academic links never do. A blocked iframe shows a visible open-in-new-tab link. Configure frame-ancestors for approved hosts including the institution's entire embedding chain. Grant only required frame permissions. Do not combine arbitrary untrusted same-origin content with a permissive sandbox. Keep local files/data in the user's browser. Check origin and source window and validate every message against the protocol, restrict payload size, match nonce and requestId, and reject commands before handshake. Set explicit targetOrigin [MSG]. A null/file origin uses an in-process offline host, not wildcard trust. No executable content in imported configuration; parse CSV as data, neutralise spreadsheet formula injection on export of text fields.

Release Deployment and acceptance
Website Standalone deep link and iframe must show identical state, work by keyboard and recover from disallowed embedding. Atlas remains useful with blocked third-party cookies.
Offline course Precache complete versioned assets over HTTPS after course download [OFFLINE], mark ready only after checksum verification; handle quota and stale versions. Managed offline package can use localhost origin. For a genuine double-click single HTML deliverable inline dependency assets and approved datasets, avoid fetch, workers/modules that require origin, test file:// in target browser.
Lecture/tutorial Projector layout, pause/pinned comparison, permalink to a shareable scenario without student data, interactive table and printable result summary.
LMS First use deep link or allowlisted iframe with no identity. SCORM wrapper if institution needs package import and completion/score; xAPI adapter only with authorised LRS and actor policy. LTI 1.3 needs registration, platform auth, OIDC/JWT validation and a backend for graded services. H5P can wrap surrounding content, with separate cross-origin event bridge. [SCORM, XAPI, LTI, H5PX]

Start staging with only the declared origin, anonymous sessions and local export. Test failure cases: no network after offline download, blocked storage, missing version, malformed input, old recipe state, message from wrong origin and iframe unable to embed. If release changes results, publish a new immutable version and preserve old assets. Roll back catalogue pointers only. Re-run paired tests before class use.

Recipe Lab, Master and FlexBench integration

A .furm equipment profile describes equipment and tag configuration. Proposed independently versioned educational recipes may point to the same profile and the same simulation model. Academic content selects restrictions, scenario and evidence requirements. The block never imports an Author project or assumes an attached PLC. Introduce a mapping adapter only when the relevant profile, channel and unit conventions have been inspected in the actual software.

Host Inputs and ownership Evidence / completion
Website Default scenario and selected model variant. Anonymous, browser-local state. Optional CSV/state export. A lecture can be unguided.
Recipe Lab Exact simulation and scenario version, visible/hidden/locked controls and outputs, narrower bounds, prediction prompt, scenario events and overlay target IDs. Predicate tree with explicit units, tolerances, duration or explanation evidence. Resume by exact state/version; an author can choose no assessment.
Master Simulation Simulation-only input mapping, declared engineering units, simulated time, run/source flags. Master keeps process-operation ownership. Compare virtual traces against the same educational model; never mistake synthetic tags for a physical run.
Master + FlexBench Read-only archived CSV first. Future adapter resolves approved semantic channels from a .furm profile and device metadata. Predicted pump duty vs measured duty, with time-window selection, instrument resolution, geometry, speed basis and uncertainty.
University LMS Hosted iframe or course package; later opt-in SCORM, xAPI or LTI. Only authorised completion/score events leave the page. Server-side verification is necessary for high-stakes grading.

Concrete pump path. In EXP01 have the student predict head at two flows and save a curve with assumptions. In EXP02 show how a valve stroke changes system resistance; a loss coefficient is not identical to actuator position. In EXP03 select series or parallel and predict the installed duty. Compare to an independent physical run with aligned pump speed and valve setting. In EXP04 ask whether saturation, sensor lag or plant response explains the trace. A pump command percentage is not RPM or measured shaft power.

Use CSV channels time_s, flow_m3_s, p_suction_Pa and p_discharge_Pa as proposed canonical names; actual headers require a mapping preview. Declare absolute/gauge reference, time zone or monotonic origin, sensor tap heights, actual inside diameters, density and speed. Compute measured head H=(pd−ps)/(ρg)+(vd²−vs²)/(2g)+zd−zs. Gauge readings using the same reference may be differenced. Differently referenced gauges need correction. Reject missing units and unlabelled timestamps; retain excluded points and reasons. Never infer pump efficiency from speed command. Compare EXP01 fit against different runs, not rows withheld from the same quasi-steady window.

Anchors and overlays. Each block publishes logical IDs, role, label and optional repeatable entity ID; e.g., S11/material_layer_1, S06/boundary_layer_profile, S09/pump_operating_point. Resolve to current SVG/DOM node or accessible equivalent at render time. On mobile a collapsed graph can return an affordance to reveal it. Rename only with migration alias. Missing required anchors block scenario launch with diagnostic; optional ones fall back to their textual description. Overlay highlight is reversible, keyboard-focusable and scoped to the instance.

Privacy and interoperability. Anonymous starter state omits name, email, LMS identifiers and device tracking. Save locally only on explicit action, permit export/delete, explain that browser storage can be cleared. Import teaching data with local processing; inspect and remove identifying free text. University integration requires data minimisation, explicitly authorised purposes, access controls, retention period, hosting location, deletion and institutional privacy review [PRIV]. For H5P the outer package licence and each asset licence are recorded independently. A static iframe alone does not grant identity, score submission or access to cross-origin H5P events.

Curriculum, prioritisation and implementation

Each ID has one controlled specification. “Extension” denotes a scoped investigation requiring separate scientific review before release. A qualitative comparison does not authorise a quantitative readout. Defined extension exercises

Internal convection. Add a separate S14 tube preset with smooth circular fully developed laminar flow, constant properties and negligible axial conduction, viscous dissipation and buoyancy. For a constant wall temperature NuD≈3.66, for constant wall heat flux NuD≈4.36. Inlet temperature, thermal development length and boundary type are required; do not apply either to an entrance region or to a flat plate. At kf=.60 W/(m K) and D=.020 m these give h≈109.8 or 130.8 W/(m² K). Screen hydrodynamic and thermal entrance lengths, not Re alone. For natural convection S52 displays Ra and calls for an orientation/BC-specific law rather than inferring h from the forced-flow model. [HEAT]

Variable conductivity. For one slab with k(T)=k₀[1+a(T−Tref)] and fixed face temperatures, q″=[∫Tc^Th k(T)dT]/L. For k₀=1 W/(m K), a=.01 K⁻¹, Tref=300 K, Tfaces 300/320 K, L=.1 m, heat flux magnitude=220 W/m². Reject nonpositive conductivity anywhere on the interval. Linear T(x) is then generally wrong. Recover it by integrating k(T) and solving for T at each x. [HEAT]

Stage efficiency. S23 counts an equilibrium partial reboiler separately. If only overall tray efficiency Eo is supplied for an illustration, actual trays=ceil((Nideal−1)/Eo), plus the separate reboiler; no stage for total condenser. With six ideal contacts and Eo=.70 use eight trays plus the reboiler. Murphree stage efficiencies instead use local composition changes; a single efficiency and this shortcut are inadequate for rigorous tray rating. [SEP, MCC]

Coefficient fitting. Compare a straight line with a power correlation Nu=a Reᵇ fit within measured conditions. Log-space regression changes the implied noise model. Use a direct nonlinear fit for additive errors in Nu; inspect residual and upper/lower-domain holdouts. NIST Norris verifies linear regression; Gauss2 tests numerical least-squares convergence and has a different functional form. Neither dataset supplies convection coefficients. [STRD, STAT]

Natural convection and commissioning uncertainty. For a temperature-controlled vertical plate, calculate RaL with properties at film temperature. A future vertical-plate model may use the Churchill–Chu average Nu relation; shipping it requires the chosen original formulation, correct Rayleigh range, geometry, uncertainty and sign-off. If a supplied h comes from a mixed or forced flow, show it as an input with provenance. Keep passive/conductive heat transfer distinct from mechanical circulation. [HEAT]

Prerequisites, cross-subject reuse and practical pathways

Read left to right within each pathway. Cross-subject prerequisites are skill dependencies rather than mandated course enrolments. Reuse a pure kernel when geometry, independent variables and boundary conditions agree. S07 supplies the Reynolds concept across pipe, plate, impeller and particle flows; each variant defines its own characteristic scales and regime criteria.

Full prioritisation and weights

Score each criterion 1 (least favourable), 3 (moderate), 5 (most favourable), with 2 and 4 intermediate. Difficulty is student conceptual difficulty; higher means more reason to intervene. Build, verification and computation ease are reverse-burden scores. Alternative gap describes incremental value beyond a strong existing free option, not evidence of demand. Product/academic judgements, not market measurements. Weighted score = Σ(weight × score)/5 out of 100. Ties sorted by stable ID. Every component is in the CSV. Reweight by multiplying component columns by a new 100-point vector. Expansion ratings use subject-level priors adjusted for known rig links/advanced methods; revisit as lecturers score individual blocks.

Six implementation tracks and first release

Relative effort uses small (1), medium (2–3) and large (4–5) block estimates, assuming reusable UI and model tools exist. Effort points compare work; do not convert to a fixed delivery date before the shared kernel and two representative blocks have shipped. Scientific and educational review is additional to coding. The numerical priority score is evidence for selection, not a sequence that can ignore prerequisites.

Track Recommended sequence Entry / exit condition Dominant risk
Initial website Versioned shell, unit/validity engine, state plus graph/scene; vertical slice S11 wall and S02 continuity; add S03, S07, S04, S05, S08 and S09 along the hydraulic path Exit when both vertical slices work offline/standalone and embedded, saved predictions replay, unsupported regimes suppress affected estimates and a lecturer completes a keyboard-only exercise. Add comparator modules after base gates. Distributed state or misleading diagrams; compare equation, graph and export from one calculation revision.
Expanded undergraduate S01 early authoring companion; S26/18 then S21/19/20; S06/14, S13/17, S15, S22/23; S33–63 and other subject blocks by semester demand Each block passes analytical/solver, applicability, curriculum and device gates. Pilot a transfer problem outside the first example before scaling authoring effort. Numerical breadth outruns review capacity; reuse mechanisms and release small subject packs.
Equipment design S10 after S08/09, then S12, S16, S20, S23, S24; S47, S60, S63, S65, S75/76/79 as data mature Each design has independent basis, forward/inverse checks, at least one infeasible case, explicit equipment limits and trade-off table. False precision in selection and costs; identify required vendor confirmation.
Advanced numerical S26 and regression/uncertainty S27/28; S32 then S58, S66/68, S77; add workers/WASM only after profiling Manufactured/analytic references, mesh and timestep evidence and stable replay; profile worst allowed case on target device. Solver failure or false complexity; test near singular/branch transitions.
Experimental integration S09/S08 first on EXP01/02, S45 on EXP03, S25 on EXP04. Later passive tracer S19/57 and heat exchange with correct bath basis Independent measurement, documented sensor units/timebase, held-out service window, uncertainty and correction history. Uncertain geometry or confounded calibration; retain unknown status when evidence is missing.
Recipe Lab and LMS Prove block init/restore/lock/anchor events from a mock host now. Later add Recipe Lab editor/adapters, scoped Qt/lectures and LMS commitments. One immutable model serves two lessons with different hidden variables and evaluation; feature compatibility and migration tested with old recipes. Coupling lessons to physical screen positions or a single equipment profile.

First delivery gate. S11 proves the term-to-material interaction, discontinuous interface temperature and independent sizing exercise without relying on hardware data. S02 proves SI conversions, constrained controls and an independent second physical scene. S09 demonstrates commercial relevance once hydraulic prerequisites exist. These also give three different failure classes (interface physics, inconsistent inputs, no operating point). Keep authoring manual until authors repeat the same activity enough times to justify tooling.

Indicative shared effort. Discovery and reviewed contracts 3–5 shared points; kernel/units/validity 5–8; accessible diagram, graph and math components 5–8; embed/offline/snapshot 3–5; CSV with data lineage 3–5; independent QA fixtures and browser matrix 3–5. These are scope-relative estimates, not prices or staffed sprints. Re-estimate against actual effort after S11/S02 and a single WP staging deployment.

Deliverables A–L

Furmtech Chemical Engineering Interactive Simulation Library · specification baseline 0.1.0 · 25 November 2026.

The first public product is an independent educational website collection. A simulation block owns its scientific model and state. Learning activities choose what to reveal and assess. Furmtech Author continues to configure equipment; Master operates it; Master Simulation provides virtual environments; Recipe Lab can later sequence and overlay educational blocks. A physical rig is optional for learning and essential for claims about that rig’s behaviour.
