A–P specification template

One owner per simulation ID. Record a model version, educational content version, data revision, review status, affected host adapters and superseded versions. Allocate new IDs for distinct reusable models; a change of teaching activity usually warrants a new scenario.

Section Mandatory review questions
A Identification What stable ID, subject, primary A–F, model tag(s), academic level, duration, effort and scope apply?
B Educational purpose What observable outcome, prerequisite, misconception, industrial use and experiment justify an interactive scene?
C Mathematics Which signed equations, symbols, units, constants, material properties, IC/BC and derivation establish the prediction? Identify independent, fixed, constrained and calculated quantities.
D Controls For each ID specify name/symbol, meaning, canonical and display units, min/max/default/step, linear/log scale, permitted combinations, locked/derived states and accessible input mechanism. Include mode-specific target controls.
E Outputs Specify IDs, units, intermediate values, rounding vs tolerance, physical interpretation, provenance, uncertainty and flags.
F Scene What exactly moves or changes when an input changes? Specify named geometry, orientation, quantitative vs qualitative marks, legend, magnification and semantic targets.
G Graphs What axes, units, scales, bounds, traces, references, markers, bands and experimental overlays answer the question? Provide a table equivalent.
H Interactive equations Give symbolic → substituted → intermediate → rounded result, unit consistency and term-focus links.
I Applicability Which assumptions are stipulated, observed, unknown or violated? Specify the rule, consequence, alternative and outputs affected.
J Alternatives Simplest useful model, additional mechanism/data/solver cost, experimental identifiability and when a decision would change.
K Design State target, controlled variables, discrete catalogue or continuous domain, feasibility checks, nonuniqueness, objective trade-off and detailed engineering boundary.
L Learning Explore, predict and investigate, independent challenge, misconceptions and feedback, transfer/extension and assessment evidence.
M V&V Source-backed analytical/published reference, independent check, limiting/invalid cases, units, residuals, numerical convergence/tolerances; separately identify physical comparison data and uncertainty.
N Implementation Algorithm and complexity, dynamic step independent of rendering, ledger of dependencies, offline/browser/mobile/a11y/performance and custom graphics needs.
O Integration Scenario pins, exposed/hidden/locked fields, anchors, completion rule, capture, state round trip, CSV mapping and host capabilities.
P Readiness Links/sections, licences, illustrative/empirical sources, open questions, owner, review stage, dependency, priority and next learning.

Categories are A mathematical foundations, B physical phenomena, C analytical engineering models, D unit operations, E design/sizing and F advanced modelling/judgement. Fidelity tags F1–F6 are a separate classification. Difficulty is conceptual; computational cost and implementation effort are separate quantities.

Measured-data example

NIST's Norris file contains 36 observed ozone-monitor calibration pairs; the original text columns are response y first, predictor x second. Read both columns without assigning invented physical units or treating the sequence as time. Use this reference case in S27 to verify coefficient orientation and residual calculations. Source data and certified values are available from NIST. Raw file · Certified fit

Quantity Recalculated by QR on 36 observations NIST certified
Intercept -0.26232307377413 −0.262323073774029
Slope 1.00211681802045 1.00211681802045
Residual sum of squares 26.6173985294231 26.6173985294224
Residual standard deviation, 34 df 0.8847963961444 0.884796396144373

Implementation. Build A=[1,x], compute thin QR, solve Rβ=Qᵀy, compute residuals using the original x units and s=√(SSE/34). Compare coefficients to absolute tolerance 1e−10 and SSE to 1e−9. The overlay should offer fitted response and a residual axis with a zero line; a near-unity slope on the main plot can conceal deviations on the residual plot. Keep the mean confidence band and future observation interval distinct. This dataset benchmarks the fitting procedure on observed measurements. It supplies no calibration for a Furmtech sensor or pump.

The downloadable source data are linked above. The reference chart in the reading edition is an original rendering of these published observations.

Controlled simulation specifications

S01 · Rate, gradient and accumulated volume · prototype · F1

A · Identification

S01 · specification 0.1.0 · Mathematics · primary category A · Introductory · F1 · effort 2/5 · 8–15 min. Maturity: specification drafted. Prototype implementation brief.

B · Educational purpose

At what instant is a vessel filling fastest? Move a tangent and two time cursors on the same trace. Students often read the height of a flow trace as its accumulated volume.

Dragging the same time cursor reveals how instantaneous slope and cumulative area answer different questions.

Outcome: Determine b for a target volume given m and endpoints; zero duration makes the inverse unidentifiable. Challenge: equal final flows can have different inventories. Prerequisites: No additional block required. Understand / Apply. Lecture demo, tutorial, guided or independent web activity, pre/post-lab. Practice link: Flow logging or weighed accumulation; EXP01 optional. Industrial teaching context: Model construction and data analysis.

C · Mathematical basis

Q(t)=b+mt; dQ/dt=m; V(t)−V(0)=bt+mt²/2. Use the signed difference of the antiderivative at the two cursors. Initial inventory zero for the default example.

Independent quantities and engineering units appear below. Outputs are derived. Assume SI absolute state variables unless a quantity is explicitly a difference or a gauge reading. Algebraic variants use the listed boundary state and require no time initialisation.

D · Inputs and controls

ID Quantity / symbol SI or scaled Alternative Min Max Default Step Scale Control
b Initial flow b m³/s L/min 0.0 0.01 0.002 0.0001 linear slider + numeric
m Ramp slope m m³/s² same -0.0001 0.0001 2e-05 1e-06 linear slider + numeric
t End time t s min 0.0 100.0 50.0 1.0 linear slider + numeric
a Start time a s min 0.0 100.0 0.0 1.0 linear slider + numeric

Mode selector: ramp (default), sampled. Design target volume .125 m³ (0–1, step .005); with a=0,t=50,m=.00002 solve b=.002. Disable b while solving.

Bounds are teaching controls. Apply the physical and mode constraints in C and I after checking finite values, ranges and integral counts. Keep inactive mode inputs locked; update derived fields from the same committed transaction. Model coefficients and initial conditions fixed in C/I are read-only in this baseline.

E · Model outputs

q[m³/s], slope[m³/s²], volume[m³]

Display three significant figures by default, counts as integers; provide inspectable full precision and a unit-labelled data table. Pair each output with applicability and provenance. Show uncertainty as unknown unless an input budget, fitted interval or identified measurement uncertainty is available.

F · Physical visualisation

Draw tank inventory and an adjustable secant approaching the tangent. Two keyboard-movable cursors bound a hatched signed area. Map slope to tangent orientation, never to liquid level. Anchor flow_area.

Semantic targets: S01/flow_area, S01/tangent, S01/end_cursor. Link focus from each target to its quantity and text alternative.

G · Graphical outputs

t [s] against Q [m³/s] and a separate aligned accumulation [m³]; optionally graph estimated derivative versus t. Fix y scale during comparisons.

Start with a linear scale unless explicitly marked logarithmic. Use computed domain of the allowed sweep, freeze scale for pinned comparisons, expose bounds and units. Use separate symbols for measured, fitted and calculated series. Include a numerical table equivalent.

H · Interactive mathematics

Render the symbolic relationship in C, a live numerical substitution using D, the intermediate terms and the selected result in E. Selecting flow_area focuses its diagram or graph and the corresponding term. Worked comparison: At default Q=.003 m³/s, slope=.00002 m³/s², V=.125 m³. With a=t area=0. Halving step leaves trapezoidal integral exact for a straight line.

I · Assumptions and applicability

Linear ramp, continuous commanded flow; reject a>t. Negative Q is an outward flow, suppress a physical fill animation if the integral demands negative inventory. Compare sampled trapezoids and noisy forward differences.

Apply per-output within/approaching/outside/unknown rules. Record assumed facts separately from verified input evidence. Unmodelled physical states or invalid dimensions suppress the corresponding output.

J · Model alternatives and fidelity

Fit b,m from time-stamped scale readings; differences amplify high-frequency noise.

Starter cost: direct scalar evaluation per rendered sample. Escalate when the omitted mechanism changes the decision by more than the uncertainty in the comparison, and when the additional data can be identified. See the fidelity and correlation standards for F-tag and evidence scope.

K · Engineering judgement and design

Determine b for a target volume given m and endpoints; zero duration makes the inverse unidentifiable. Challenge: equal final flows can have different inventories.

Document the target, remaining degrees of freedom, active constraints and feasible alternatives. Compare any inverse result by forward substitution; preserve infeasibility and multiple solutions. Cost requires a dated independent basis; use the physical trade-off otherwise.

L · Learning activities

Explore. At what instant is a vessel filling fastest? Move a tangent and two time cursors on the same trace. Students often read the height of a flow trace as its accumulated volume.

Investigate. Commit a prediction before changing a control. Change b and leave m fixed. The slope is unchanged because b translates the graph. Compare two ramps with the same integrated volume.

Challenge and assessment. Determine b for a target volume given m and endpoints; zero duration makes the inverse unidentifiable. Challenge: equal final flows can have different inventories. Submit a result with units, one rejected interpretation and the condition that would change the answer. Extension: Fit b,m from time-stamped scale readings; differences amplify high-frequency noise.

M · Verification and validation

At default Q=.003 m³/s, slope=.00002 m³/s², V=.125 m³. With a=t area=0. Halving step leaves trapezoidal integral exact for a straight line.

Verify dimensions and either an independent analytical limit, conservation identity or alternative numerical solve. Reject non-finite inputs and out-of-domain combinations in I. Use unrounded references; tolerances and regression process are in the QA standard. One independently computed prototype fixture is included in verification/reference_results.json. Physical validation requires independent observations in the declared domain; synthetic reference cases establish no equipment accuracy.

N · Software implementation

Closed-form evaluation plus exact primitive; for secant width h>0 clip endpoints to domain. Sample 101 x coordinates only for rendering.

Compose reviewed kernels and scene primitives; use a small custom adapter for any model-specific geometry. Use event-driven evaluation for parameter changes, fixed simulation sample clock for dynamics, 10–20 Hz text/plot refresh and pausable scene. Package locally, support responsive SVG/table alternatives and the common in-process/iframe contract. Downsample display only.

O · Furmtech integration

Scenario pins S01 and model version, locks selected variables, may hide the main output until prediction, and targets flow_area. Save the state and pre-reveal prediction, accept a completion event on a checked result and explanatory evidence. Flow logging or weighed accumulation; EXP01 optional. Import measured data with units, calibration and provenance. Master consumes a read-only model snapshot; same block runs in a standalone tutorial or LMS embed.

P · References and development readiness

  • [FNC] Driscoll and Braun, Fundamentals of Numerical Computation. Consult chapters on linear least squares, roots, IVPs, BVPs and diffusion. Reference only. https://fncbook.com/

Priority 85.6/100, rank 19; Expanded undergraduate. Starter scope can be prototyped against the supplied fixture. Open: real-system data, independent academic sign-off, per-asset reuse permissions and production browser tests. S02 · Continuity through a contraction · prototype · F1

A · Identification

S02 · specification 0.1.0 · Fluids · primary category C · Introductory · F1 · effort 2/5 · 8–15 min. Maturity: specification drafted. Prototype implementation brief.

B · Educational purpose

Pinch a pipe while holding throughput fixed. Predict which cross-section has greater mean velocity and whether mass flow changes.

Changing the section without changing parcel throughput makes the diameter-squared relationship visible.

Outcome: Choose a bore to meet a velocity ceiling at fixed delivery; report feasible available bores. Explain why shrinking a real nozzle on a fixed pump may change Q. Prerequisites: No additional block required. Understand / Apply. Lecture demo, tutorial, guided or independent web activity, pre/post-lab. Practice link: EXP01 measured flow and line geometry. Industrial teaching context: Piping, pumping and metering.

C · Mathematical basis

A=πD²/4; v=Q/A; ṁ=ρQ. Two stations share Q by steady incompressible continuity. Positive axial direction downstream. Density fixed at 1000 kg/m³.

Independent quantities and engineering units appear below. Outputs are derived. Assume SI absolute state variables unless a quantity is explicitly a difference or a gauge reading. Algebraic variants use the listed boundary state and require no time initialisation.

D2 Downstream bore D₂ m mm 0.01 0.1 0.025 0.001 linear slider + numeric

Mode selector: fixedThroughput (default), boreDesign. Velocity cap 2 m/s (.25–4, step .05); Q=.001 gives Dmin=√(4Q/πvmax)=.0252313 m. Round up to a catalogue bore if required.

S03 · Hydrostatic pressure and datum · prototype · F1

A · Identification

S03 · specification 0.1.0 · Fluids · primary category B · Introductory · F1 · effort 1/5 · 8–15 min. Maturity: specification drafted. Prototype implementation brief.

B · Educational purpose

Lower a pressure tap and switch the display between absolute and gauge pressure. A wider vessel feels intuitively heavier but does not change the pressure at a fixed depth.

A single moving tap reveals which part of a pressure change comes from depth and which from the reference datum.

Outcome: Infer depth from gauge reading allowing nonatmospheric surface pressure; unknown surface pressure makes the inverse nonunique. Prerequisites: No additional block required. Understand / Apply. Lecture demo, tutorial, guided or independent web activity, pre/post-lab. Practice link: Static water-column pressure check; EXP01 tap-datum preparation. Industrial teaching context: Piping, pumping and metering.

C · Mathematical basis

dp/dz=−ρg with z upward; p_abs=p_surface+ρgh for depth h down from the free surface. g=9.80665 m/s²; local atmosphere for gauge display fixed at 101325 Pa.

S04 · Bernoulli and the mechanical energy balance · prototype · F2

A · Identification

S04 · specification 0.1.0 · Fluids · primary category C · Intermediate undergraduate · F2 · effort 3/5 · 12–22 min. Maturity: specification drafted. Prototype implementation brief.

B · Educational purpose

Given a narrowing pipe that rises, predict the downstream tap reading. Toggle losses to discover which head is dissipated and which terms can be recovered.

Moving elevation or bore separately shows which head terms exchange and which losses dissipate mechanical energy.

Outcome: Choose pump head to recover a required outlet pressure; explain the difference between pressure recovery and energy dissipation. Introduce measured losses for a real rig. Prerequisites: S02 Continuity through a contraction, S03 Hydrostatic pressure and datum. Apply / Analyse. Lecture demo, tutorial, guided or independent web activity, pre/post-lab. A · Identification

Move a probe downstream and explain why the layer thickens while local wall shear decreases. Compare local quantities with length averages on the same plate.

A · Identification

S08 · specification 0.1.0 · Fluids · primary category C · Advanced undergraduate · F3 F4 · effort 4/5 · 20–35 min. Maturity: specification drafted. Prototype implementation brief.

B · Educational purpose

Trace a pipe operating point onto the Moody axes; roughness changes can matter very differently at two flow rates.

The point on a Moody diagram moves while the device displays a pressure difference, making the friction factor an observable engineering consequence.

Outcome: Solve required head for each available bore; compare fixed-f assumption and roughness sensitivity. Use bisection on s=1/√f over [1,30], residual <10⁻¹⁰. v=4Q/(πD²); Δp=fD (L/D)ρv²/2 where fD is the Darcy factor; laminar fD=64/Re; turbulent 1/√fD=−2log₁₀[ε/(3.7D)+2.51/(Re√fD)]. ρ=1000 kg/m³, μ=.001 Pa·s.

B · Educational purpose

Move a material interface and change its conductivity separately. Thickness changes resistance; the intrinsic conductivity of a homogeneous constant-property material stays fixed.

Changing thickness without changing material separates conductivity from resistance and splits interface drops visibly.

Outcome: Choose minimum L₂ to meet a heat-flux limit within a depth constraint; flag already feasible and impossible cases. Repeat with a worse contact and explain the interface temperatures. A · Identification

S12 · specification 0.1.0 · Heat transfer · primary category E · Intermediate undergraduate · F2 · effort 3/5 · 12–22 min. Maturity: specification drafted. Prototype implementation brief.

B · Educational purpose

Add insulation to a small isothermal cylinder. Predict the sign of the first change in heat loss before seeing the curve.

Dragging the outer radius through the maximum exposes two possible thicknesses for one heat-loss target.

Outcome: Bracket on each side of rc, report all thicknesses for a target magnitude; impose any space cap after solving. At zero driving force no unique insulation design. S13 · Transient heating and cooling · prototype · F1 F4

A · Identification

S13 · specification 0.1.0 · Heat transfer · primary category C · Intermediate undergraduate · F1 F4 · effort 3/5 · 12–22 min. Maturity: specification drafted. Prototype implementation brief.

B · Educational purpose

Compare the surface of a thick slab with its centre. A good exponential fit to one sensor does not by itself establish uniform temperature.

Centre, surface and average traces make the lumped assumption testable across a changing Biot number.

Outcome: Solve elapsed time to a target strictly between initial and ambient. Reach equilibrium asymptotically; do not return a finite time at exactly ambient. Prerequisites: S01 Rate, gradient and accumulated volume, S11 Fourier conduction through a composite wall. Apply / Analyse. Lecture demo, tutorial, guided or independent web activity, pre/post-lab. Practice link: Proposed thermal module; instrumented slab for spatial validation. Industrial teaching context: Thermal processing and heat exchange.

C · Mathematical basis

Infinite slab of half-thickness L, two identical convecting faces, Lc=V/As=L. Bi=hL/k, α=k/(ρcp), Fo=αt/L²; lumped T=T∞+(Ti−T∞)exp[−h t/(ρcp L)]. For distributed comparator solve ∂T/∂t=αTxx; Tx(0)=0, −kTx(L)=h(Ts−T∞), initial T=Ti. ρcp=2.0×10⁶ J/(m³ K).

Independent quantities and engineering units appear below. Outputs are derived. Assume SI absolute state variables unless a quantity is explicitly a difference or a gauge reading. Algebraic variants use the listed boundary state and require no time initialisation.

A · Identification

S15 · Heat exchanger performance and flow arrangement · prototype · F2

A · Identification

S15 · specification 0.1.0 · Heat transfer · primary category D · Intermediate undergraduate · F2 · effort 3/5 · 12–22 min. Maturity: specification drafted. Prototype implementation brief.

B · Educational purpose

Reverse the cold stream while keeping both inlet conditions fixed. Compare the cold outlet with the hot outlet and the local approach temperature.

Reversing one stream lets learners inspect both terminal approach temperatures before interpreting the outlets.

Outcome: Choose the arrangement for a required duty and explain when terminal outlet temperatures can cross without local reversal. A bucket with a submerged coil is a different bath boundary condition. Prerequisites: S11 Fourier conduction through a composite wall, S14 Convection from a plate and the Nusselt number. Apply / Analyse. Lecture demo, tutorial, guided or independent web activity, pre/post-lab. Practice link: Proposed heat-exchanger module; confirm stream vs bath boundary. C · Mathematical basis

Ch=ṁh cp,h; Cc=ṁc cp,c; Cr=Cmin/Cmax; N=UA/Cmin; εparallel=[1−exp(−N(1+Cr))]/(1+Cr); εcounter=[1−exp(−N(1−Cr))]/[1−Cr exp(−N(1−Cr))]. At Cr=1 counter ε=N/(1+N). Q̇=εCmin(Thi−Tci); Tho=Thi−Q̇/Ch, Tco=Tci+Q̇/Cc.

S16 · Heat exchanger area and feasible duty · prototype · F2 F4

A · Identification

S16 · specification 0.1.0 · Equipment design · primary category E · Advanced undergraduate · F2 F4 · effort 3/5 · 20–35 min. Maturity: specification drafted. Prototype implementation brief.

B · Educational purpose

Move a duty target towards the maximum and observe why area grows rapidly. Diagnose an infeasible request before entering the root solver.

An approaching temperature pinch makes the asymptotic area requirement visible before a solver reports failure.

Outcome: Enumerate both layouts, filter area cap, report Pareto between required area and assumed fouling margin; simulate achieved duty after rounding area upward. Utilities require their own flow/temperature basis. Prerequisites: S15 Heat exchanger performance and flow arrangement. Evaluate / Create. Lecture demo, tutorial, guided or independent web activity, pre/post-lab. Practice link: Proposed heat-exchanger module, preliminary duty exercise. Industrial teaching context: Preliminary equipment selection.

C · Mathematical basis

From target Q̇ calculate terminal temperatures using Ch,Cc. For counterflow ΔT₁=Thi−Tco, ΔT₂=Tho−Tci; for parallel use inlet and outlet differences. ΔTlm=(ΔT₁−ΔT₂)/ln(ΔT₁/ΔT₂), limit ΔT₁=ΔT₂. A=Q̇/(Udirty ΔTlm); 1/Udirty=1/Uclean+Rf″.

S17 · Diffusive flux and transient concentration · prototype · F1 F2

A · Identification

S17 · specification 0.1.0 · Mass transfer · primary category B · Introductory · F1 F2 · effort 3/5 · 8–15 min. Maturity: specification drafted. Prototype implementation brief.

B · Educational purpose

Distinguish a steady gradient through a membrane from a front entering an initially uniform medium. Doubling thickness and doubling time have different effects.

Switching the boundary-value problem changes the shape of the entire profile, from a line to a moving diffusive front.

Outcome: Choose steady barrier thickness to limit flux, then explain why using that relation for breakthrough time is unjustified. Prerequisites: S01 Rate, gradient and accumulated volume, S11 Fourier conduction through a composite wall. Understand / Apply. Lecture demo, tutorial, guided or independent web activity. Practice link: Independent tracer diffusion or membrane coupon demonstration. Industrial teaching context: Diffusion, drying and gas–liquid transfer.

C · Mathematical basis

Steady J=−D(C₂−C₁)/L. Semi-infinite transient C(x,t)=Ci+(Cs−Ci)erfc[x/(2√(Dt))], C(0,t)=Cs, C(∞,t)=Ci. In transient mode C₁=Cs and C₂=Ci; at t=0 handle surface jump separately.

B · Educational purpose

A learner can distinguish the instantaneous flow imbalance from the accumulated level change.

Outcome: Find capacity required over a pulsed feed sequence; or determine gravity equilibrium (Qin/CdAo)²/(2g) and check vessel limits. Compare level-only vs separate outlet data. S23 · McCabe–Thiele design and reflux · prototype · F2 F4

A · Identification

S23 · specification 0.1.0 · Separations · primary category E · Advanced undergraduate · F2 F4 · effort 5/5 · 20–35 min. Maturity: specification drafted. Prototype implementation brief.

B · Educational purpose

Step stages graphically, then move reflux toward pinch and explain why an apparently small change can make a finite design impossible.

Each click links one equilibrium contact to a stage and reveals how steps crowd at a pinch.

Outcome: Compare reflux vs stages at same purity and feed. No energy/cost ranking until latent heat/feed rate/utility prices supplied. Stage efficiency and flooding require additional models/data. Prerequisites: S22 Binary vapour–liquid equilibrium. Evaluate / Create. Lecture demo, tutorial, guided or independent web activity. Practice link: Graphical design tutorial; no physical column claimed. Industrial teaching context: Separation and purification.

C · Mathematical basis

y*=αx/[1+(α−1)x]; xeq(y)=y/[α−(α−1)y]. Rectifying y=Rx/(R+1)+xD/(R+1); saturated-liquid q-line x=zF. Stripping line through (zF,yrect(zF)) and (xB,xB). Start (xD,xD), go horizontally to equilibrium then vertically to active line using x≥zF as rectifying. Stop after horizontal step reaches x≤xB.

S25 · PID control, saturation and recovery · prototype · F4

A · Identification

S25 · specification 0.1.0 · Control · primary category D · Advanced undergraduate · F4 · effort 5/5 · 20–35 min. Maturity: specification drafted. Prototype implementation brief.

B · Educational purpose

Apply an unreachable setpoint and release it. Observe commanded output, delivered output and integral state separately.

Unclamped demand, delivered signal and integral state diverge during saturation and reunite during recovery.

Outcome: Tune for settling time, overshoot and time saturated on fixed scenarios, compare achievable and unreachable demands; multiple tunings meet requirements. EXP04 uses measured flow and actual controller settings. Prerequisites: S18 Dynamic tank mass and level balance, S26 Numerical integration and timestep convergence. Apply / Analyse. Lecture demo, tutorial, guided or independent web activity, pre/post-lab. Practice link: EXP04 PID flow control. Industrial teaching context: Process operation and control.

C · Mathematical basis

Synthetic plant τdy/dt=−y+Kpu+d. Each sample e=r−y; D=−Kc Td (y−yprev)/Ts filtered with β=Tf/(Tf+Ts), Df=βDfprev+(1−β)D; uraw=Kc e+I+Df; u=clip(uraw,0,1). I_next=I+Ts[Kc e/Ti+(u−uraw)/Tt] when back-calculation enabled. Plant exact ZOH update y_next=Kpu+d+(y−Kpu−d)exp(−Ts/τ). τ=10 s, Kp=1, Tf=.5 s, Tt=2 s, Ts=.1 s. Normalised variables.

A · Identification

S27 · specification 0.1.0 · Mathematics · primary category F · Advanced undergraduate · F4 F6 · effort 4/5 · 20–35 min. Maturity: specification drafted. Prototype implementation brief.

B · Educational purpose

Fit a calibration line, reveal held-out points, and decide whether curvature or scatter is the larger problem. A high R² can coexist with poor extrapolation.

Predictive spread, mean confidence and holdout residuals respond differently to more measurements.

Outcome: Choose smallest dataset and degree with acceptable held-out error; optional curved truth y=1+2x+x² demonstrates bias. Compare fit under interpolation and shifted-domain validation. Teaching line y=a+bx+ε; use QR least squares on [1,x]. s²=SSE/(n−2); leverage h*=1/n+(x*−x̄)²/Sxx; 95% mean CI: ŷ±t(.975,n−2)s√h*; prediction interval uses √(1+h*). Extension quadratic fit via QR on centred/scaled x and independent hold-out residuals.

C · Mathematical basis

Fresh A and inert I enter a first-order pass with fixed conversion X. Remove all product, return fraction 1−p of unreacted A and I. Aloop=FA/[1−(1−p)(1−X)]; Iloop=FI/p. Bypass alternative treats fraction b of fresh feed as untouched, Xoverall=(1−b)X at no recycle.

B · Educational purpose

Separate loss of resolution due to retention shift from band broadening.

Peak height can change at constant area.

Outcome: Separate loss of resolution due to retention shift from band broadening. Prerequisites: S27 Fitting an empirical correlation, S57 Tracer residence time and nonideal mixing. Apply / Analyse. Two Gaussian peaks with baseline widths wi=4σi; Rs=2(tR2−tR1)/(w1+w2), area-normalised Gaussian concentration signal. N=(tR/σ)² for ideal plate model.

S84 · Mixing time, heat production and scale evidence · expansion · F2 F6

A · Identification

S84 · specification 0.1.0 · Bioprocess · primary category F · Advanced undergraduate · F2 F6 · effort 4/5 · 20–35 min. Maturity: specification drafted. Expansion specification; optional variants require detailed review before coding.

B · Educational purpose

Compare scaled tanks using mixing time, cooling margin and independent oxygen transfer rather than one criterion.

A single probe reaching tolerance does not establish whole-vessel mixing.

Outcome: Compare scaled tanks using mixing time, cooling margin and independent oxygen transfer rather than one criterion. Prerequisites: S57 Tracer residence time and nonideal mixing, S72 Dissolved oxygen and competing oxygen demand, S75 Mixing vessel, agitation power and scale-up. Analyse / Evaluate. Lecture demo, tutorial, guided or independent web activity, pre/post-lab. Practice link: Proposed food-yeast or abiotic classroom dataset. Industrial teaching context: Biochemical unit operations.

C · Mathematical basis

Fit a first-order tracer envelope e(t)=∣C−C∞∣/∣C₀−C∞∣=exp(−t/τm); t95=τm ln20. Separate energy balance ρcp V dT/dt=Qgen−UA(T−Tc); Qgen specified, not inferred from agitation.

Independent quantities and engineering units appear below. Outputs are derived. Assume SI absolute state variables unless a quantity is explicitly a difference or a gauge reading. Algebraic variants use the listed boundary state and require no time initialisation.

D · Inputs and controls

ID Quantity / symbol SI or scaled Alternative Min Max Default Step Scale Control
tau Tracer decay time τₘ s min 1.0 100.0 10.0 1.0 linear slider + numeric
q Heat generation Q𝗀 W kW 0.0 500.0 100.0 1.0 linear slider + numeric
UA Cooling conductance UA W/K same 5.0 100.0 20.0 1.0 linear slider + numeric

Bounds are teaching controls. Apply the physical and mode constraints in C and I after checking finite values, ranges and integral counts. Keep inactive mode inputs locked; update derived fields from the same committed transaction. Model coefficients and initial conditions fixed in C/I are read-only in this baseline.

E · Model outputs

mixing_time[s], steady_temperature_rise[K], heat_load[W]

Display three significant figures by default, counts as integers; provide inspectable full precision and a unit-labelled data table. Pair each output with applicability and provenance. Show uncertainty as unknown unless an input budget, fitted interval or identified measurement uncertainty is available.

Synchronise multiple tracer probe histories, mixing tolerance band and thermal load bars. Display empirical vs synthetic labels.

Semantic targets: S84/equipment_view, S84/operating_point. Link focus from each target to its quantity and text alternative.

time vs dimensionless tracer deviation and bulk temperature rise
